facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with new and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy
Two years earlier, he had undergone a wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
An incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved, with no evidence of distant metastatic disease
no evidence of distant metastatic disease
Multiple satellite lesions appeared
He received 4 cycles of ipilimumab
new lesions appeared
Multiple satellite lesions were present on the left posterior auricular scalp area
clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation were noted
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
CD163 and myeloperoxidase: Highlighted histiocytes and neutrophils respectively

concepts.why: The patient presented with new and progressive satellite lesions, which is consistent with melanoma recurrence.
The patient's histopathology results showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate, which is consistent with an immune-mediated inflammatory response.
The patient had a history of melanoma and presented with multiple satellite lesions, which is consistent with dermal melanoma metastasis.
The patient received ipilimumab and developed an inflammatory infiltrate, which is consistent with an ipilimumab-induced inflammatory reaction.
The patient received pembrolizumab and developed an inflammatory infiltrate, which is consistent with a pembrolizumab-induced inflammatory reaction.
The patient presented with multiple satellite lesions, which is consistent with melanoma with satellite lesions.
The patient's histopathology results showed a neutrophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate, which is consistent with neutrophilic dermatitis.
The patient's lesions showed clinical regression and persistent black pigmentation, which is consistent with tumor regression.
It explains the fact that there was no evidence of distant metastatic disease, which is consistent with the diagnosis of Stage III Melanoma.
